docs.text: HardFOC board HAL Vortex V1 HAL ¶ The software layer for the HardFOC Vortex V1 motor controller board. One Vortex object gives your ESP32-C6 application the TMC9660 motor controller, encoders, the IMU, temperatures, ADC channels, GPIO, CAN, storage and a status LED, through a small set of managers that know the board's wiring. Quickstart Architecture Source on GitHub This repository ( hf-hal-vortex-v1 ) turns the board into C++ objects. Your application does not touch GPIO numbers or SPI frames; it calls vortex.motors , vortex.encoders , vortex.temp . Single-axis motor controller board Vortex V1 HardFOC MCU ESP32-C6 (RISC-V, Wi-Fi 6, BLE, 802.15.4, TWAI); ESP-IDF release/v5.5 Motor controller TMC9660: integrated gate drivers, on-chip FOC current, velocity and position loops; BLDC, stepper or brushed DC; host link UART 115200 baud (default) or SPI2 Sensors AS5047U 14-bit magnetic angle encoder slot (SPI2) · BNO08x 9-axis IMU (I2C) · NTC thermistor on TMC9660 AIN3 I/O PCAL95555 16-bit I2C expander: TMC9660 control lines, IMU boot and reset, CAN standby, power good Communication CAN 500 kbit/s (TWAI) · I2C 100 kHz · USB Serial/JTAG (console, flashing) Power Motor supply, needed only to spin a motor; the board starts and logs from USB without it Status One WS2812 RGB LED Hardware · Pin map Vortex V1 HAL, layer by layer Figure description and sources From top to bottom, each layer only calls the one under it. Your application asks the facade singleton for the managers. The managers (one per board function) own the hf-core handlers, which wrap one chip driver each; a manager may also use a driver directly. Drivers talk to hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, whose ESP32 implementations sit on ESP-IDF. Every name in a band is read from the code: the managers from the facade's member references, the handlers, drivers and interface classes from the managers' and handlers' #include lines. Drawn from: lib/api/Vortex.h Vortex (manager references) ; lib/managers #includes ; lib/core/handlers #includes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/hal-layers.py . What you get ¶ One Vortex object that brings the board up in a fixed order and reports what failed ( Initialisation ). One manager per board function: motor, encoders, IMU, ADC, temperature, GPIO, LED, communication, storage ( Managers ). The TMC9660 over UART or SPI, with unit-aware motor- and load-frame velocity and position, and every TMCL parameter through visitDriver() ( MotorController ). A pin map generated from the board's pin header, across the ESP32-C6, the PCAL95555 and the TMC9660 ( Pin map ). Diagnostics for every manager: GetLastError() , health snapshots, statistics dumps ( Errors and diagnostics ). Example and bench apps for every chip, most built by CI on every pull request ( Examples ). Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Install ESP-IDF, clone with submodules, build, flash and watch the first example. Bring-up and troubleshooting The first power-up, step by step, and what each start-up failure means. Hardware Buses, chips and the pin map, generated from the board's pin header. Architecture Layers, start-up order, ownership, threading and errors. Managers One page per manager: what it does, its API, an example and its pitfalls. docs.text: Bring-up and troubleshooting ¶ How to bring a new Vortex V1 board up one chip at a time, and what to do when a step fails. If your problem is not here, the start-up log usually names the manager that failed; start from that manager's page. Bring up a new board ¶ Work from the cheapest check to the most expensive, and do not connect a motor until the steps before pass. Each app is built and flashed as in the quickstart ( ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor <app> Release from examples/esp32 ). USB only, no motor supply. Flash vortex_api_test . NVS, Comms, GPIO and LEDs must be OK : they are required, and EnsureInitialized() returns false without them. FAIL on Motors, ADC or Temp is expected here. I2C devices. Flash vortex_i2c_scan_pcal_bno_pca : the PCAL95555 and the BNO08x must answer on the shared I2C bus. vortex_pcal_gpio_imu_bringup adds full I2C diagnostics when one does not. LED. Flash vortex_led_ws2812_smoke : the WS2812 runs its colour demo. Motor supply, no motion. Connect the motor supply and flash vortex_motor_comms_smoke : it reads back the TMC9660 control lines on the PCAL95555, brings the TMC9660 out of its bootloader and reads telemetry without moving anything. Then vortex_bldc_telemetry_sweep checks the power-stage configuration. First spin. Follow the bench guides before you run any vortex_bldc_* motion app: the BLDC bring-up guide (bootloader and parameter-mode order) and the bench matrix (per-app goals, supply and safety notes). vortex_bldc_open_loop_uart is the confirmed-working open-loop spin. Bench limits live in one file Supply, shunt, current caps, I²t and thermal limits for every bench app are in vortex_bench_safety.hpp . Check them against your motor and supply before step 5. Build ¶ Symptom Cause Fix fatal: not a git repository or empty lib/core Submodules not initialised git submodule update --init --recursive APP_TYPE not defined idf.py build run directly Build with ./scripts/build_app.sh <app> <Debug|Release> No supported board variant defined! The pin-map selector got no HARDFOC_BOARD_* define Build through this repository's CMake; it defines HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 Errors in ESP-IDF headers Wrong ESP-IDF version or target Use release/v5.5 and esp32c6 ( Get started ) Start-up ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Vortex API initialization failed A required step failed: NVS, comms, GPIO or the LED Read the error just above it. NVS already erases and retries a full or outdated partition; if it still fails, check that the partition table has an nvs partition Initialized in degraded mode — Motors:OFF ... A best-effort manager did not start Expected without a motor supply or with parts not fitted; otherwise check that manager's wiring Motors, ADC and Temp all OFF together The onboard TMC9660 did not come up; ADC and two temperature sensors depend on it Check the motor supply and the TMC9660 control lines on the PCAL95555 IMU OFF No answer at 0x4A, or reset / boot lines not driven Run vortex_i2c_scan_pcal_bno_pca ; check PCAL_IMU_RST and PCAL_IMU_BOOT Stack overflow in main during start-up Main task stack too small Keep CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=8192 or more Running ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Encoder reads return NOT_INITIALIZED No device created vortex.encoders.CreateAs5047uDevice(0, SpiDeviceId::AS5047U_POSITION_ENCODER) LED blink or breath does not move Nobody calls UpdateAnimation() Call it every 50 ms from a task SetOnboardTmc9660Transport ignored in the log Called after EnsureInitialized() Call it before GPIO call returns GPIO_ERR_PIN_NOT_FOUND Name typo, or a core / comm pin Copy the name from the pin map ; only GPIO-category pins are registered The monitor shows only waiting for download The port was reopened in download mode Pass --no-reset to ./scripts/idf_flash_monitor.sh , or press reset Documentation ¶ Symptom Fix CI says a generated region or figure is stale hardfoc-docs gen && hardfoc-docs figures , then commit mkdocs build --strict reports a link Fix the link; links to code outside docs/ work as relative paths

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ This page takes you from nothing to a Vortex V1 board printing its start-up log. Each step says how to tell that it worked. Plan on half an hour, most of it the ESP-IDF download. What you need ¶ Item Notes A Vortex V1 board The board starts and logs over USB alone USB cable Data-capable; the ESP32-C6 enumerates as a USB serial / JTAG device A motor supply Only to spin a motor. Without it the motor manager comes up degraded, which is expected Linux, macOS or Windows (WSL2) The build scripts are Bash 1. Install ESP-IDF ¶ The examples target esp32c6 and build with ESP-IDF release/v5.5 (both read from examples/esp32/app_config.yml , which CI uses too). mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp git clone -b release/v5.5 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32c6 . ./export.sh It worked if idf.py --version prints a v5.5 version. Run . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh in every new terminal. 2. Clone with submodules ¶ The HAL pulls the shared core ( lib/core : handlers, drivers, the pin map), the build scripts and CANopenNode as git submodules. git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-hal-vortex-v1.git cd hf-hal-vortex-v1 If you already cloned without submodules: git submodule update --init --recursive It worked if ls lib/core/handlers lists handler folders and ls examples/esp32/scripts shows build_app.sh . One submodule is private docs/hf-development-handbook is a private repository and is marked update = none , so the recursive update skips it. You do not need it to build. 3. Build an example ¶ Every example is an "app" selected by name. Start with vortex_api_test , the default app, which initialises the whole HAL and exercises each manager. cd examples/esp32 ./scripts/build_app.sh list # every app name ./scripts/build_app.sh vortex_api_test Release # build one It worked if the script ends with a successful link and a build folder named after the app, the build type and the target appears under examples/esp32/ . 4. Flash and monitor ¶ Connect the board over USB, then: ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor vortex_api_test Release Set ESPPORT first if more than one serial port is present (for example export ESPPORT=/dev/ttyACM0 ). Leave the monitor with Ctrl + ] . It worked if the log shows Vortex API initialization completed successfully in ... ms followed by a Component Status line with OK or FAIL for each of NVS, Comms, GPIO, Motors, ADC, IMU, Encoders, LEDs and Temp. FAIL on Motors, ADC or Temp without a motor supply is normal: those steps are best effort. See Initialisation . 5. Use the HAL in your own code ¶ #include "api/Vortex.h" #include "managers/LedManager.h" #include "managers/TemperatureManager.h" extern "C" void app_main () { auto & vortex = Vortex :: GetInstance (); if ( ! vortex . EnsureInitialized ()) { return ; // NVS, comms, GPIO or the LED failed: nothing below can work } ( void ) vortex . leds . IndicateReady (); float chip_c = 0.0f ; if ( vortex . temp . ReadInternalTemperature ( chip_c ) == hf_temp_err_t :: TEMP_SUCCESS ) { // chip_c is the ESP32-C6 die temperature } } Next ¶ Architecture explains the layers under Vortex . Examples lists every app and what it shows. Bring-up and troubleshooting covers a new board and the common first-day problems.

docs.text: Roadmap ¶ Where the Vortex V1 HAL is going, and the known gaps in what is here today. Nothing on this page is a promise of a date; it is the order of work as currently planned. CANopen device ¶ The next large piece of work is making Vortex V1 a CiA 402 servo drive node on its CAN port: one object dictionary as the single source for firmware, EDS file and tools; CANopenNode v4 behind a narrow stack interface; the TMC9660's own loops doing the motion while the ESP32-C6 runs the CiA 402 state machine, limits and faults; and host tests that run the same node against a simulated motor. What Where State CANopen node design: CiA 301 / 402 drive, object dictionary as the single source, threads, wireless access, CAN FD route canopen-node.md Draft, under review Drive observability: every TMC9660 parameter, telemetry and fault in the object dictionary, the CLI and a dashboard drive-observability.md Draft, under review Header-only contracts (CAN frame, CiA 402 rule table, fault policy, router policy, OD store) with host tests contracts/ in hardfoc-vortex-v1 Merged Notes on the current CAN path, hf-utils-canopen and the TMC9660 canopen.md Published CANopenNode sources third_party/CANopenNode (submodule), built with the HAL's Build CANopenNode slave stack option Present The HAL's part is small by design: the CAN port stays a BaseCan* from CommChannelsManager , and the drive talks to the TMC9660 through MotorController . Another MCU and CAN FD ¶ A future Vortex is expected on an STM32 with CAN FD. ADR 0001 records the boundary that makes this a port of four managers rather than a rewrite, and lists what crosses it today. Known gaps ¶ Gap Where Page Most managers allocate with throwing make_unique , so a failed allocation aborts lib/managers ADR 0002 ESP32 port numbers and gpio_num_t in managers CommChannelsManager.cpp , LedManager.h ADR 0001 Only some managers build on the host (the rest still construct ESP32 peripherals themselves) tests/host/seams Testing and CI hf-core NtcTemperatureHandler recurses until the stack overflows when enable_threshold_monitoring is set in its config; the HAL applies the window after init instead hf-core handlers/ntc TemperatureManager

docs.text: Writing these docs ¶ How pages, figures and generated tables are made, so that the site stays true to the code. Preview the site ¶ python3 -m pip install "git+https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme" mkdocs serve Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 . mkdocs build --strict is what CI runs: a broken link, a missing image or an image without alt text fails it. Write a page ¶ Say what the page is for in its first sentence, then answer it. Prefer short sections, tables and numbered steps. Link to code with a relative path, as GitHub resolves it ( ../lib/api/Foo.h ); the site rewrites the link to the file on GitHub at the commit that was built. Link to the API reference under api/ ( ../api-reference.md explains it); the link is checked on the built site, after the API is merged. Use admonitions ( !!! note , !!! warning ) for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration. A new folder gets an index.md ; docs/.nav.yml orders the top tabs. Add a figure ¶ A figure is a Python module in docs/diagrams/figures/ . It extracts its facts from the code in data() , lists the files they come from in "sources" , and lays them out in build(data) with figkit ( from hardfoc_mkdocs_theme.figkit import Fig ). The module docstring's Reads: paragraph is the figure's long description; the alt sentence is required. hardfoc-docs figures # writes docs/diagrams/<id>.svg, <id>.dark.svg, figures.json hardfoc-docs figures --check # what CI runs Embed it on a page with a marker pair; the build fills it in: <!-- figure: docs-pipeline --> <!-- /figure --> The build refuses a figure whose text is below 4.5:1 contrast in either theme, whose content does not fit, or whose cards overlap. Light and dark are the same layout, so they cannot drift apart. Add a generated table ¶ A generator is a module in tools/docs/generators/ with a REGIONS dict from a region name to a function that returns Markdown. Mark the region on a page and run hardfoc-docs gen ; CI runs it with --check : <!-- generated: my-table --> <!-- /generated --> Record a decision ¶ Copy the ADR template to the next number in docs/adr/ and add it to the table in Decisions .

docs.text: ADR 0001: Keep the MCU behind the interface wrap; only managers know the board ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ HardFOC boards share chips (the TMC9660, AS5047U, BNO08x, WS2812, CAN) and a common core ( hf-core : handlers, drivers, interface wrap). Vortex V1 runs on an ESP32-C6 today. A future Vortex is expected on an STM32 with CAN FD, and the CANopen device work planned for the board is meant to move with it unchanged. The motor, sensor and protocol code must not be tied to ESP-IDF. Options ¶ Write the HAL directly against ESP-IDF. Fast to start; every manager and handler would need rewriting for another MCU. Put the MCU behind interface classes and keep board knowledge in one layer. Chip drivers and handlers use only BaseSpi , BaseI2c , BaseGpio , BaseAdc , BaseCan , BaseUart , BaseNvs , BaseTemperature ; the managers are the only code that knows which chip is on which pin of which board. Decision ¶ Option 2. The boundary is: Drivers and handlers (in hf-core ) depend only on the Base* interface classes. The ESP32 implementations ( EspSpiBus , EspI2cBus , EspUart , EspCan , EspGpio , EspNvs , EspTemperature ) are named only in the managers that create buses and peripherals: CommChannelsManager , GpioManager , NvsManager and TemperatureManager . The generated manager map lists every manager's interface classes, read from the #include lines. Board wiring lives in the per-board pin map in hf-pincfg ( ADR 0003 ). Application code sees managers, handlers and Base* pointers (for example BaseCan* from GetCanOpenBus() ), never Esp* types. Consequences ¶ A port to another MCU replaces the Esp* construction in those four managers with another implementation of the same interfaces (the Stm* classes in the interface wrap are the start of one) and adds a pin map; handlers, drivers and code above the managers stay. CAN FD fits the same seam: an FD-capable BaseCan implementation (frames up to 64 bytes, data-phase bit timing) is created by CommChannelsManager instead of EspCan . Code that only sees BaseCan* keeps working; code that wants FD frames checks the port's capabilities. BaseCan 's message type still carries 8 data bytes, so enlarging it is the first step of an FD port. Known leaks across the boundary today, to fix before a port: LedManager uses the ESP-IDF RMT WS2812 driver and returns a gpio_num_t ; CommChannelsManager.cpp writes ESP32 port numbers (SPI host 1, I2C_NUM_0 , UART port 1); examples/esp32 call ESP-IDF directly, which is fine for examples.

docs.text: ADR 0002: Allocate once at start-up; fixed tables, no growing containers ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design, with the exceptions listed) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ The board drives a motor for long periods. Heap fragmentation or an allocation failure in the middle of a control loop is hard to diagnose and can leave the drive in an unknown state. On the other hand, which chips answer is only known at start-up, external devices are added by the application, and some objects (bus drivers, chip drivers) are easiest to create on the heap. The examples build with C++ exceptions off. Options ¶ Everything static. No heap at all; every driver object a member. Rigid, and some driver classes are not designed for it. Allocate during start-up and device creation, never in a read, write or control call. Tables with a known size are fixed arrays; objects whose existence depends on start-up results are created on the heap and kept for the program's life. Allocate freely. Simple, and the problems above. Decision ¶ Option 2: Tables are std::array sized at compile time: the GPIO and ADC entries (from the pin map), the SPI device table ( SpiDeviceId::DEVICE_COUNT ), the handler slots ( MAX_TMC9660_DEVICES , MAX_IMU_DEVICES , MAX_ENCODER_DEVICES , all 4), the bounded runtime I2C slots, and the facade's diagnostics arrays ( kVortexManagerCount ). Bus objects, handlers and drivers are held in std::unique_ptr (GPIO pins in std::shared_ptr , because their owners differ), created when the owning manager initialises or when you create a device. No manager allocates in its read, write, motion or LED calls. Consequences ¶ After Vortex::EnsureInitialized() , and once your own devices are created, the motor, ADC, temperature, GPIO, encoder, IMU and LED paths do not touch the heap. Where this is not strictly true today: Run-time device creation allocates: CreateI2cDevice() , MotorController::CreateExternalDevice() , ImuManager::CreateExternalBno08xDevice() , EncoderManager::CreateAs5047uDevice() . Create devices during your own start-up. Most managers use std::make_unique / std::make_shared ; with exceptions off, an allocation failure aborts instead of failing initialisation. Only TemperatureManager uses hf::utils::make_unique_nothrow . ImuManager::ConfigureInterrupt() stores a std::function , which may allocate for a capturing callback. Allocations inside ESP-IDF and the chip drivers are not covered by this decision.

docs.text: ADR 0003: The hf-pincfg X-macro table is the single source of pin truth ¶ Status Accepted (records the current design) Date 2026-11-01 Context ¶ A pin number written in more than one place drifts: the schematic changes, one copy is updated, another is not, and the board misbehaves in a way no compiler catches. Vortex V1 spreads its pins over three chips (ESP32-C6, PCAL95555, TMC9660), which makes copies even easier to get wrong. Pin numbers used to be repeated in this repository's README and docs. Options ¶ Pins as constants in each manager. Simple; every manager and every document repeats them. One table per board, used by the code and by the docs. The board's functional pin map in hf-pincfg ( hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp ), written as X-macro rows; everything else reads it. Decision ¶ Option 2: Each row of HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST / HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_CHANNEL_LIST names a function, its chip, unit, pin, polarity, pull, drive and current. The same rows generate the enums, name tables and mapping arrays. The managers register from the generated arrays: GpioManager creates a pin for each GPIO-category row on whichever chip it is, AdcManager a channel for each ADC row; CommChannelsManager and the facade look pins up by HfFunctionalGpioPin ( GetGpioMapping() , gpio.Get(...) ). No manager writes a GPIO number. The pin map page and the board figure are generated from the same rows ( hardfoc-docs gen , hardfoc-docs figures ), and CI fails if they are stale. Consequences ¶ Changing a pin is one edit in hf-pincfg , a submodule bump here, and a docs rebuild. The pin map is shared by every HardFOC HAL through hf-pincfg ; the board is chosen at build time with HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 (set in this repository's CMakeLists.txt ). The examples that call ESP-IDF directly get their GPIO numbers from vortex_board_pins.hpp , which reads them from the pin map at compile time and static_assert s that each net is an ESP32 pin; there is no second copy.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the Vortex V1 HAL is put together. The short version: your code talks to one object, Vortex ; Vortex holds one manager per board function; managers own hf-core handlers; handlers wrap chip drivers; drivers reach the hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, which sit on ESP-IDF. Vortex V1 HAL, layer by layer Figure description and sources From top to bottom, each layer only calls the one under it. Your application asks the facade singleton for the managers. The managers (one per board function) own the hf-core handlers, which wrap one chip driver each; a manager may also use a driver directly. docs.text: Errors and diagnostics ¶ The HAL does not throw: the examples build with C++ exceptions off, every call is noexcept and failure comes back in the return value. This page lists the error types, where to read the last error, and the system diagnostics. Rules of thumb ¶ Check the return value. Most methods are [[nodiscard]] ; the compiler warns if you drop a result. A method that returns bool returns false on failure; a method that returns a pointer returns nullptr when the manager is not initialised or the thing you asked for does not exist. Every manager has GetLastError() . Prefer the value a call returns: the last error is shared by every caller of that manager and may already describe a later call. Error types by manager ¶ Manager Error type To text NvsManager hf_nvs_err_t (set on initialisation) HfNvsErrToString() CommChannelsManager CommError CommErrorToString() GpioManager hf_gpio_err_t HfGpioErrToString() MotorController MotorError MotorErrorToString() AdcManager hf_adc_err_t HfAdcErrToString() ImuManager ImuError ImuErrorToString() EncoderManager EncoderError EncoderErrorToString() LedManager LedError LedErrorToString() TemperatureManager hf_temp_err_t HfTempErrToString() The board-specific enums ( CommError , MotorError , ImuError , EncoderError , LedError ) start with SUCCESS (0), then NOT_INITIALIZED , then manager-specific values. The hf_*_err_t types come from the interface wrap and are shared with every HardFOC board. System diagnostics ¶ All of these are on the Vortex object. CollectManagerHealth() and PerformHealthCheck() return false until EnsureInitialized() has succeeded. Call Gives you GetSystemDiagnostics(VortexSystemDiagnostics&) Which managers initialised, how many failed (and their names), start-up time, uptime; system_healthy GetComponentInitializationStatus() std::array<bool, 9> , one flag per manager GetFailedComponents(out, max) Names of managers whose initialisation failed CollectManagerHealth(ManagerHealthSnapshot&) Per manager: initialised, has an error, last error code (as uint8_t ), and an overall all_healthy PerformHealthCheck() Logs the health snapshot and returns whether all managers are healthy ( false before initialisation) DumpSystemStatistics() Logs every manager's statistics GetSystemUptimeMs() , GetInitializationTimeMs() , GetSystemVersion() Timing and the HAL version string The last error code in a health entry is the manager's own enum cast to uint8_t ; read it with the table above. docs.text: Initialisation ¶ Vortex::EnsureInitialized() brings every manager up, one at a time, in a fixed order. Call it once, early in app_main() , before you touch any manager. Vortex::EnsureInitialized() Figure description and sources Left to right, then the second row. The facade initialises the managers one at a time, in the order of the calls in its init function. The first group is required: if any of them fails, EnsureInitialized() returns false and the application should not continue. The second group is best effort: a failure there is logged as a warning, the manager stays unavailable and the system reports itself as degraded, so a bench with only some chips fitted still comes up. The order and the required / best-effort split are read from the init function, which returns false only in the required branches. Drawn from: lib/api/Vortex.cpp Vortex::InitializeAllComponents ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/init-order.py . The order ¶ From Vortex.cpp ( Vortex::InitializeAllComponents ); do not edit. Step Manager Member If it fails 1 NvsManager vortex.nvs initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 2 CommChannelsManager vortex.comms initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 3 GpioManager vortex.gpio initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 4 LedManager vortex.leds initialisation fails ( EnsureInitialized() returns false) 5 MotorController vortex.motors warning; the system runs degraded 6 AdcManager vortex.adc warning; the system runs degraded 7 ImuManager vortex.imu warning; the system runs degraded 8 EncoderManager vortex.encoders warning; the system runs degraded 9 TemperatureManager vortex.temp warning; the system runs degraded The order follows the dependencies: storage first, so configuration and calibration can be read early; then the buses; then the GPIO pins, which include the PCAL95555 expander lines the TMC9660 needs; then the status LED, early so an LED-only bench works without the motor controller. After that come the managers that depend on the TMC9660: AdcManager reads its channels through the TMC9660, and TemperatureManager reads the NTC through AdcManager and the chip temperature from the TMC9660. What happens when a step fails ¶ Required steps (NVS, comms, GPIO, LEDs). If one fails, EnsureInitialized() logs an error, stops and returns false . IsInitialized() stays false , and calling EnsureInitialized() again retries from the start. Best-effort steps (motors, ADC, IMU, encoders, temperature). A failure is logged as a warning and the manager stays unavailable; the remaining steps still run and EnsureInitialized() returns true . The log then says Initialized in degraded mode and lists which of Motors, ADC, IMU, Enc and Temp are OFF . Check vortex.motors.IsInitialized() (or the diagnostics ) before relying on a best-effort manager. This lets a bench with only some chips fitted, or with the motor supply off, still come up and log. The onboard TMC9660 and its transport ¶ Step 5 creates the onboard TMC9660 before initialising MotorController . It takes the four TMC9660 control lines (reset, driver enable, fault, wake) from GpioManager , which is why GPIO comes first, and registers the chip on one of two host links: Transport How to select it What happens UART (default) nothing TMCL over the UART at TMCL address 1; the SPI mux pin PCAL_TMC_SPI_COMM_EN stays released SPI Vortex::SetOnboardTmc9660Transport(VortexOnboardTmc9660Transport::Spi) before EnsureInitialized() TMCL over SPI2; MotorController asserts the SPI mux while it talks to the chip SetOnboardTmc9660Transport() is ignored (with a warning) once initialisation has completed. Calling a manager directly ¶ Every manager has its own EnsureInitialized() , which returns true at once if the manager is already up. Code that uses one manager on its own can call it, but going through Vortex::EnsureInitialized() gives the right order, the onboard TMC9660 registration and the system diagnostics. EncoderManager creates no device by itself; see EncoderManager . Shutting down ¶ Vortex::Shutdown() de-initialises every initialised manager, in this order: temperature, LEDs, encoders, IMU, ADC, motors, GPIO, comms, NVS. That is the start-up order reversed except for the LED manager, which is shut down second although it starts fourth. It then clears the initialised flag, so a later EnsureInitialized() starts again from the beginning. It returns false if the HAL was not initialised.

docs.text: Ownership ¶ Who creates each object, who owns it, and how memory is allocated. The short version: the facade owns nothing but references; each manager is a singleton that owns its handlers and bus objects for the life of the program; other managers borrow them. Managers, handlers and drivers Figure description and sources Managers on the left, hf-core handlers in the middle, chip drivers on the right. An arrow means "includes and uses": a manager owns or borrows the handler it points at, and each handler wraps exactly one driver. Several managers share the TMC9660 handler, because that one chip provides motor control, GPIO, ADC channels and a temperature sensor; MotorController owns it and the others reach it through MotorController. LedManager uses its driver directly, without a handler. Managers with no arrow (communication buses, NVS) talk to the interface wrap only. Drawn from: lib/managers #includes ; lib/core/handlers #includes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/manager-dependencies.py . Managers, handlers and drivers ¶ From the #include lines of lib/managers and the hf-core handlers; do not edit. Manager Uses managers hf-core handlers (driver) Drivers used directly Interface classes AdcManager MotorController tmc9660 (hf-tmc9660) - BaseAdc CommChannelsManager - - - BaseCan , BaseI2c , BaseSpi , BaseUart , EspCan , EspI2c , EspSpi , EspUart EncoderManager CommChannelsManager , GpioManager as5047u (hf-as5047u) - BaseGpio , BaseSpi GpioManager CommChannelsManager , MotorController pcal95555 (hf-pcal95555), tmc9660 (hf-tmc9660) - BaseGpio , EspGpio ImuManager CommChannelsManager , GpioManager bno08x (hf-bno08x) - BaseGpio , BaseI2c , BaseSpi LedManager - - hf-ws2812-rmt - MotorController CommChannelsManager , GpioManager tmc9660 (hf-tmc9660) - - NvsManager - - - BaseNvs , EspNvs TemperatureManager AdcManager , MotorController ntc (hf-ntc-thermistor), tmc9660 (hf-tmc9660) - BaseTemperature , EspTemperature Singletons ¶ Every manager is a function-local static ( GetInstance() , a Meyers singleton): it is constructed on first use and never destroyed. So vortex.motors and MotorController::GetInstance() are the same object; prefer the facade in application code so the start-up order is respected. docs.text: Threading ¶ What you can safely call from more than one FreeRTOS task. The HAL creates no tasks of its own : every call runs in the task that makes it. Periodic work, such as LED animation steps, is driven by your code. Locks ¶ Lock order, when one manager calls another while holding its own lock: MotorController → GpioManager (the TMC9660 SPI mux line is a PCAL95555 pin), and a manager's lock → its handler's lock. Nothing takes them in the other order. Each manager (except NvsManager ) has one RtosMutex from hf-utils-rtos-wrap . Still call it from app_main() before you start other tasks: it blocks for the whole bring-up. ADC, temperature, LED and motor configuration calls may be made from several tasks; the manager serialises them. A call can block while another task holds the lock (for example during an SPI or UART transfer). GPIO calls are serialised by the manager lock, so two tasks cannot interleave a configuration change on the same pin. A read-modify-write of your own (read, decide, write) still needs one owner task. SPI2 is shared by the TMC9660 (when on SPI), the AS5047U and the external slots. The examples set CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=8192 in sdkconfig.defaults ; keep at least that much if you initialise from app_main() .

Vortex V1: buses and chips ¶ Vortex V1: buses and chips Figure description and sources The ESP32-C6 on the left runs all the software. Each arrow to the right is one bus or signal, labelled with the GPIOs it uses: SPI2 to the TMC9660 motor controller and the AS5047U encoder (plus two external chip selects), a UART that is the TMC9660's default host link, I2C to the PCAL95555 I/O expander and the BNO08x IMU, TWAI to the CAN transceiver, and one data line to the WS2812 status LED. The PCAL95555 drives the TMC9660 control lines (driver enable, reset, wake, SPI mux) and the IMU's boot and reset lines, and reads their fault and interrupt outputs. The layout is drawn by hand; every GPIO number, expander bit, chip select, SPI mode and I2C address is read from the functional pin map and the comms manager, so a pin change rebuilds this figure. Your application asks the facade singleton for the managers. The managers (one per board function) own the hf-core handlers, which wrap one chip driver each; a manager may also use a driver directly. Drivers talk to hardware only through the interface classes of the internal interface wrap, whose ESP32 implementations sit on ESP-IDF. Every name in a band is read from the code: the managers from the facade's member references, the handlers, drivers and interface classes from the managers' and handlers' #include lines. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What is on the Vortex V1 board, as the software sees it: one ESP32-C6, the buses it drives and the chips on each bus. Every pin number on this page comes from the board's functional pin map; the full tables are on the pin map page. Vortex V1: buses and chips Figure description and sources The ESP32-C6 on the left runs all the software. Each arrow to the right is one bus or signal, labelled with the GPIOs it uses: SPI2 to the TMC9660 motor controller and the AS5047U encoder (plus two external chip selects), a UART that is the TMC9660's default host link, I2C to the PCAL95555 I/O expander and the BNO08x IMU, TWAI to the CAN transceiver, and one data line to the WS2812 status LED. The PCAL95555 drives the TMC9660 control lines (driver enable, reset, wake, SPI mux) and the IMU's boot and reset lines, and reads their fault and interrupt outputs. The layout is drawn by hand; every GPIO number, expander bit, chip select, SPI mode and I2C address is read from the functional pin map and the comms manager, so a pin change rebuilds this figure. Drawn from: lib/core/hf-core-drivers/internal/hf-pincfg/src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST ; lib/managers/CommChannelsManager.h SpiDeviceId ; lib/managers/CommChannelsManager.cpp add_builtin_device ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/board-overview.py . The chips ¶ Chip What it does Bus Manager that owns it ESP32-C6 RISC-V MCU with Wi-Fi 6, BLE, 802.15.4 and TWAI (CAN); runs the HAL and your application - all of them TMC9660 Motor controller with integrated gate drivers and its own FOC current, velocity and position loops; also provides GPIO, ADC channels and a chip temperature UART (default) or SPI2 MotorController AS5047U 14-bit magnetic angle encoder SPI2 EncoderManager BNO08x 9-axis IMU with on-chip sensor fusion I2C ImuManager PCAL95555 16-bit I2C I/O expander: TMC9660 control lines, IMU boot/reset, CAN standby, power good I2C GpioManager NTC thermistor Board temperature, read on TMC9660 input AIN3 through the TMC9660 TemperatureManager CAN transceiver Physical layer for the TWAI controller TWAI CommChannelsManager WS2812 RGB status LED RMT data line LedManager Things to know before you wire anything ¶ The TMC9660 has two host links. The UART is always connected. SPI2 reaches the TMC9660 only while the expander pin PCAL_TMC_SPI_COMM_EN (active low) selects it, because the same SPI2 lines also serve the AS5047U and the external slots. The HAL uses the UART unless you call Vortex::SetOnboardTmc9660Transport(VortexOnboardTmc9660Transport::Spi) before EnsureInitialized() . TMC9660 GPIO17 and GPIO18 appear twice in the pin map : as expander inputs ( PCAL_TMC_GPIO17_EXP_IN , PCAL_TMC_GPIO18_EXP_IN ) and as TMC9660 GPIOs ( TMC_GPIO17 , TMC_GPIO18 ). Both views see the same nets. There is no encoder fitted by default. The AS5047U chip select is wired, but EncoderManager creates no device until you call CreateAs5047uDevice() . Do not copy pin numbers from TMC9660 evaluation-kit examples. Use the pin map . docs.text: Managers ¶ A manager is the one object that owns a board function: it knows which chips and pins implement it (from the pin map), creates and owns the hf-core handlers for them, and gives you a small API. Every manager is a singleton reached through the Vortex facade. Manager Member What it gives you Start-up step CommChannelsManager vortex.comms SPI2 devices, the I2C bus, the UART to the TMC9660, the TWAI (CAN) bus required NvsManager vortex.nvs Three flash key-value namespaces: application, calibration, configuration required GpioManager vortex.gpio Every GPIO-category pin by name or enum, on the ESP32-C6, the PCAL95555 and the TMC9660 required MotorController vortex.motors The onboard TMC9660 (and up to two external ones), motor and load-frame velocity and position best effort AdcManager vortex.adc The 15 TMC9660-hosted ADC channels: currents, supply voltages, temperatures, AIN inputs best effort ImuManager vortex.imu The onboard BNO08x IMU and up to three external ones, data-ready interrupts best effort EncoderManager vortex.encoders Up to four AS5047U angle encoders, created by you best effort LedManager vortex.leds The WS2812 status LED: colours, brightness, animations, status patterns required TemperatureManager vortex.temp ESP32-C6 die, NTC thermistor and TMC9660 chip temperatures best effort Every manager has the same lifecycle calls: GetInstance() , EnsureInitialized() (idempotent), IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() (or Shutdown() for the LED manager), GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(...) and DumpStatistics() . docs.text: AdcManager ¶ Gives you every ADC channel of the pin map by name or by enum. docs.text: GpioManager ¶ Registers every GPIO-category pin of the pin map, whichever chip it is on, and lets you drive or read it by name or by enum. On Vortex V1 those pins live on three chips: the ESP32-C6, the PCAL95555 I/O expander and the TMC9660. Source: GpioManager.h . Which pins it owns ¶ At start-up it walks the pin map and registers the pins whose category is GPIO (and the user, ADC and SPI categories). Core pins (crystal, boot, USB) and comm pins (bus lines, the LED data line) are skipped; their owners configure them. The names are the Name column of the pin map , for example GPIO_PCAL_TMC_DRV_EN , GPIO_PCAL_IMU_RST , GPIO_EXT_GPIO_CS_1 . Chip Pins How they are reached ESP32-C6 The two external chip selects An EspGpio the manager creates PCAL95555 TMC9660 control and fault lines, IMU boot / interrupt / reset, CAN standby, power good, TMC9660 GPIO17/18 read-back Pin objects from the Pcal95555Handler , over I2C TMC9660 TMC_GPIO17 , TMC_GPIO18 The TMC9660 handler, registered once MotorController has created the onboard device Each pin takes its polarity from the pin map. "Active" means the asserted level, so for an active-low pin SetActive() drives it low. API ¶ Call Notes Get(std::string_view name) , Get(HfFunctionalGpioPin pin) std::shared_ptr<BaseGpio> , empty if the pin is not registered Set(name, bool active) , SetActive(name) , SetInactive(name) , Toggle(name) Return hf_gpio_err_t Read(name, bool& active) , IsActive(name, bool& active) Logical state: true means asserted (polarity applied) SetDirection , SetPullMode , SetOutputMode Reconfigure a pin at run time ConfigureInterrupt(...) , EnableInterrupt , DisableInterrupt , SupportsInterrupts Edge interrupts on pins that support them Contains(name) , Size() Lookup helpers GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(GpioSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Operation counters and the last error Example: read the TMC9660 fault line ¶ #include "api/Vortex.h" #include "managers/GpioManager.h" auto & gpio = Vortex :: GetInstance (). gpio ; bool fault = false ; if ( gpio . Read ( "GPIO_PCAL_TMC_FAULT_STATUS" , fault ) == hf_gpio_err_t :: GPIO_SUCCESS && fault ) { // the TMC9660 is signalling a fault (the line is active low; Read() reports "asserted") } In a loop, look the pin up once and keep it: auto drv = gpio.Get(HfFunctionalGpioPin::PCAL_TMC_DRV_EN); . The string calls search the table on every call. Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics() reports the number of registered pins and the total, successful and failed operation counts. DumpStatistics() logs the same, with per-pin access and error counts. Pitfalls ¶ Read() returns the logical state , not the electrical level, the same as IsActive() . For an active-low pin, true means the line is low. Set(name, true) likewise drives the pin to its active level. Expander pins are slow. Every PCAL95555 access is an I2C transfer; do not toggle them in a fast loop. MotorController owns the TMC9660 control lines. Driving PCAL_TMC_DRV_EN , PCAL_TMC_RST_CTRL or PCAL_TMC_SPI_COMM_EN yourself disables or confuses the motor controller. Pin operations are serialised , but a read-then-write sequence of your own is not atomic; give such a pin one owner task. See Threading . A wrong name returns GPIO_ERR_PIN_NOT_FOUND . Copy names from the pin map.

The BNO08x runs its own sensor fusion; this manager creates its handler (which drives the reset and boot lines on the PCAL95555) and optionally wires its data-ready interrupt. Source: ImuManager.h . Devices ¶ Index Device Created by 0 Onboard BNO08x (I2C 0x4A) ImuManager::EnsureInitialized() 1 to 3 External BNO08x You: CreateExternalBno08xDevice(index, i2c_address, speed_hz) or CreateExternalBno08xDevice(index, SpiDeviceId) API ¶ Call Notes GetBno08xHandler(index = 0) Bno08xHandler* , or nullptr GetSensor(index = 0) IBno08xDriverOps* : the driver itself (enable reports, read the latest data) CreateExternalBno08xDevice(...) , DeleteExternalDevice(index) External IMUs ConfigureInterrupt(index, callback) , EnableInterrupt , DisableInterrupt , IsInterruptEnabled , WaitForInterrupt(index, timeout_ms) Data-ready interrupt; the onboard IMU uses PCAL_IMU_INT through GpioManager IsDeviceValid , GetActiveDeviceIndices , GetAvailableDevices , GetDeviceType Device bookkeeping GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(ImuSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Health per device On the handler, Update() services the SH-2 protocol and dispatches new reports to the callback set with SetSensorCallback() ; visitDriver() runs a function on the driver under the handler's lock. GetBno08xHandler (); h != nullptr ) { // Set a callback once with h->SetSensorCallback(...), then service the device periodically: ( void ) h -> Update (); } The bench app vortex_pcal_gpio_imu_bringup and the manager test encoder_imu_test in Examples show reports being enabled and read. docs.text: Animations need a caller. The manager has no task; blink, breath, rainbow and the blinking status patterns move only when you call UpdateAnimation() (the step is 50 ms). It is a required start-up step. If the RMT channel cannot be set up, Vortex::EnsureInitialized() fails. Full white at full brightness is bright and draws current. Use SetMaxBrightness() to cap it.

docs.text: MotorController ¶ Owns the TMC9660 motor controllers: the onboard one, and up to two more on the external SPI chip selects. The TMC9660 runs the motor loops itself (FOC current, velocity and position, ramps); this manager creates its handler, manages the host link and gives you unit-aware velocity and position calls in the motor frame or, through a gear ratio, the load frame. Source: MotorController.h . Devices ¶ Index Device Created by 0 Onboard TMC9660 Vortex::EnsureInitialized() (start-up step 5), on UART by default or SPI if selected 2, 3 External TMC9660 on EXTERNAL_DEVICE_1 / EXTERNAL_DEVICE_2 You: CreateExternalDevice() The onboard device needs the four control lines on the PCAL95555 (reset, driver enable, fault, wake), which the facade takes from GpioManager . The transport is chosen with Vortex::SetOnboardTmc9660Transport() before initialisation; see Initialisation . API ¶ Call Notes handler(index = 0) Tmc9660Handler* , or nullptr if there is no device at that index visitDriver(func, index = 0) Calls func(auto& driver) with the typed TMC9660 driver (SPI or UART variant); the way to reach every TMCL parameter setMotorVelocity / getMotorVelocity , setMotorPosition / getMotorPosition Motor (rotor) frame; take a value, a tmc9660::units unit and a MotorContext setMotorMechanics(MotorMechanics) , getMotorMechanics() Gear ratio (motor turns per output turn) and output inversion setLoadVelocity / getLoadVelocity , setLoadPosition / getLoadPosition Load (output shaft) frame, through the mechanics CreateExternalDevice(cs_index, ...) , DeleteExternalDevice(cs_index) External TMC9660 over SPI or UART IsDeviceValid , GetActiveDeviceIndices , InitializeAllDevices , GetInitializationStatus Device bookkeeping GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(MotorSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Health per device A MotorContext tells the unit conversions about the motor: motor type, pole pairs, velocity sensor and encoder counts per revolution. Example: run the load shaft at 30 rpm ¶ #include "api/Vortex.h" #include "managers/MotorController.h" using :: tmc9660 :: units :: VelocityUnit ; constexpr :: tmc9660 :: units :: MotorContext kCtx { tmc9660 :: tmcl :: MotorType :: BLDC_MOTOR , 7 , // pole pairs of your motor tmc9660 :: tmcl :: VelocitySensorSelection :: DIGITAL_HALL , 0u , // encoder counts per revolution (none) }; auto & motors = Vortex :: GetInstance (). motors ; if ( motors . IsInitialized () && motors . handler () != nullptr ) { ( void ) motors . setMotorMechanics ( MotorMechanics { 10.0 , false }); // 10:1 reducer ( void ) motors . setLoadVelocity ( 30.0 , VelocityUnit :: Rpm , kCtx ); } Commanding motion assumes the TMC9660 has been configured for your motor (type, pole pairs, current limits, feedback, commutation mode). The BLDC bring-up notes and the motor bench examples ( vortex_bldc_* in Examples ) show the full sequence. Diagnostics ¶ GetSystemDiagnostics() fills MotorSystemDiagnostics : whether the manager is up, how many device slots are active and initialised, the last error, and per device whether it is active, initialised and its error count. The TMC9660's own telemetry (currents, voltages, temperatures, fault flags, every axis and global parameter) is reached through visitDriver() . How the product firmware exposes all of it through the CANopen object dictionary, a CLI and a dashboard, and what the SPI access time costs, is in the drive observability design . Pitfalls ¶ No motor manager, no TMC9660 features. If the onboard TMC9660 does not come up (for example with its supply off), step 5 fails with a warning. Everything that depends on the TMC9660 (ADC channels, the NTC and chip temperatures, TMC_GPIO17/18 ) is then unavailable too. Pick the transport before start-up. SetOnboardTmc9660Transport() after EnsureInitialized() is ignored. The SPI mux is shared. On SPI, MotorController asserts PCAL_TMC_SPI_COMM_EN around its transfers; other SPI2 users must not assume the TMC9660 is off the bus. Index 1 is not a device. External devices use the chip-select indices 2 and 3. Do not copy evaluation-kit pin numbers. Hall and ABN wiring on Vortex need not match the TMC9660 kit; use the pin map and the bring-up notes.

docs.text: NvsManager ¶ Persistent key-value storage in the ESP32-C6's flash (ESP-IDF NVS), split into three namespaces and exposed as the board-independent BaseNvs interface. It starts first, so calibration and configuration can be read before the buses come up. Source: NvsManager.h . The namespaces ¶ Accessor NVS namespace Use it for App() vortex General application keys Calibration() vortex_cal Calibration and factory tuning blobs Config() vortex_cfg Structured device configuration Each returns a BaseNvs& . Code written against BaseNvs keeps working if the storage moves to another medium. API ¶ Call Notes App() , Calibration() , Config() BaseNvs& for one namespace On a BaseNvs : SetU32 / GetU32 , SetString , SetBlob , GetSize , KeyExists , EraseKey , Commit Return hf_nvs_err_t (except KeyExists ) GetLastError() Set when initialisation fails DumpStatistics() Logs each namespace Example: count boots ¶ #include "api/Vortex.h" #include "managers/NvsManager.h" BaseNvs & app = Vortex :: GetInstance (). nvs . App (); hf_u32_t boots = 0 ; ( void ) app . GetU32 ( "boots" , boots ); // stays 0 if the key does not exist yet if ( app . SetU32 ( "boots" , boots + 1 ) == hf_nvs_err_t :: NVS_SUCCESS ) { ( void ) app . Commit (); } Pitfalls ¶ Commit. Writes are not guaranteed to reach flash until Commit() . Key length. ESP-IDF limits keys to 15 characters ( GetMaxKeyLength() ). No lock in the manager. Initialise it once (the facade does); concurrent access to one namespace relies on ESP-IDF NVS itself.

docs.text: TemperatureManager ¶ Reads the board's three temperature sources by name and gives simple statistics across them. It is up if at least one sensor works. Source: TemperatureManager.h . Sensors ¶ Name Source Needs ESP32_INTERNAL The ESP32-C6's on-chip sensor (die temperature) nothing NTC_THERMISTOR NTC thermistor on TMC9660 input AIN3, through AdcManager ( ADC_TMC9660_AIN3 ); the channel and the 0–85 °C window come from config/VortexNtcConfig.h AdcManager , so the TMC9660 MOTOR_TEMP The TMC9660's internal chip temperature MotorController API ¶ Call Notes ReadTemperatureCelsius(name, float&) , ReadTemperatureFahrenheit(name, float&) By sensor name ReadInternalTemperature(float&) , ReadNtcTemperature(float&) , ReadMotorTemperature(float&) Shortcuts for the three names GetSystemTemperatureStats(min, max, avg) Across the registered sensors GetSensorCount() , GetSensorEntry(name) Registered sensors GetLastError() , GetSystemDiagnostics(TempSystemDiagnostics&) , DumpStatistics() Counters and the last error All reads return hf_temp_err_t ; TEMP_SUCCESS is 0. Example: board and chip temperature ¶ #include "api/Vortex.h" #include "managers/TemperatureManager.h" auto & temp = Vortex :: GetInstance (). temp ; float board_c = 0.0f , chip_c = 0.0f ; const bool have_board = temp . ReadNtcTemperature ( board_c ) == hf_temp_err_t :: TEMP_SUCCESS ; const bool have_chip = temp . ReadMotorTemperature ( chip_c ) == hf_temp_err_t :: TEMP_SUCCESS ; Pitfalls ¶ Two of three sensors depend on the TMC9660. Without the motor controller only ESP32_INTERNAL reads. All TMC9660 ADC channels share one BaseAdc ( Tmc9660AdcWrapper ), which routes by channel id at read time. A handler on it must be given the channel; the NTC handler's default (channel 0) would read AIN0. The die temperature is not the board temperature. It runs above ambient with the CPU load. MOTOR_TEMP is the controller chip , not the motor winding.
